h: Snooker, Steel and a Spot of Bowling
p: Sheffield is famous the world over for one particular sporting event: every spring, the Crucible Theatre hosts the World Snooker Championship, as it has since the 1970s. If your visit lines up with it, the city centre has a special buzz, and even if it doesn't, the Crucible and the neighbouring Lyceum Theatre are worth checking for shows.

The Peace Gardens, right by the Town Hall, are a lovely spot for a sit-down, with fountains that kids love to dash through on warm days. Sheffield Botanical Gardens, a little out of the centre, has beautiful glass pavilions and well-kept gardens that are free to explore. Weston Park Museum, next to the park of the same name, is a family-friendly museum covering the city's history, art and natural world.

As for the bowling, a bit of technique goes a long way. Pick a ball that you can control comfortably, aim for the arrows on the lane rather than the pins and follow through smoothly. Mixing experienced bowlers with beginners in each team keeps things close and keeps everyone laughing.

Sheffield's Supertram network and the main railway station make it easy to get into the city centre from across South Yorkshire, so the designated driver can have a night off. Book ahead for busy weekend evenings and arrive a little early.
